project.name: Him_ides
project.description: Python and GMT scripts that reproduce the figures from a study of intermediate-depth earthquakes beneath the Himalayas, using a QuakeML earthquake catalog, station lists and fault data.

nodes.name: Figures_5-9.py
nodes.summary: Driver script that reads the Himalayan QuakeML catalog, defines study sub-regions, and produces Figures 5-9 (magnitude-time, interevent times, MFDs, migration analysis) via the temporal and migration plotting modules.

nodes.name: migration_plots.py
nodes.summary: Plotting module for earthquake migration analysis along strike and dip cross-sections, including a geographic distance helper.

nodes.name: temporal_plots.py
nodes.summary: Plotting module for temporal catalog analysis: magnitude vs time with cumulative counts, interevent time distributions, and b-value magnitude-frequency plots for sub-regions.

nodes.name: dist_calc
nodes.summary: Computes distance between two lon/lat locations.

nodes.name: plot_migration
nodes.summary: Plots earthquake migration along strike and dip profiles within a swath, with map inset and time-colored events.

nodes.name: get_cat_details
nodes.summary: Extracts origin times, coordinates, depths and magnitudes from a catalog, split by region.

nodes.name: cut_cat
nodes.summary: Selects events from a catalog falling inside a polygon of coordinates.

nodes.name: create_lines
nodes.summary: Builds a line collection connecting event times to magnitudes for stem-style plotting.

nodes.name: interevent_times_single_cluster
nodes.summary: Generates the interevent time figure for several sub-catalogs and saves it.

nodes.name: mag_vs_time_plus_cumulative
nodes.summary: Creates magnitude-versus-time plot with cumulative event counts for sub-regions (Figure 5).

nodes.name: calc_bvalues
nodes.summary: Computes b-value fit and fit function from magnitude frequency data above completeness.

nodes.name: multi_mfd_plot
nodes.summary: Plots magnitude-frequency distributions with b-value fits for multiple catalogs (Figure 7).

nodes.name: Figure_1.sh
nodes.summary: GMT shell script that draws the manuscript's Figure 1 map of the Himalayan region with topography, fault traces, seismic stations and deep earthquake catalogs (HIMNT, NSC candidates).
nodes.languageNotes: Chains GMT commands with -K/-O and heredocs to build a layered PostScript, then converts it to PDF.

nodes.name: Figure_2.sh
nodes.summary: GMT shell script that produces Figure 2, a map of deep earthquake events with topography, faults, country labels, cluster boxes and station symbols.
nodes.languageNotes: Layered GMT PostScript map built with -K/-O appends and inline heredoc data.

nodes.name: Figure_3AB.sh
nodes.summary: GMT script producing Figure 3A-B depth cross-sections of seismicity, projecting NLL and HypoDD locations onto two swaths of 50 km half-width.

nodes.name: Figure_3CD.sh
nodes.summary: GMT script producing Figure 3C-D cross-sections, projecting NLL and HypoDD locations with error bars along two profiles and cleaning temporary files.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Short instructions for creating the gmt5 conda environment and running Figure_1.sh to build the first manuscript map.

nodes.name: gmt5.yml
nodes.summary: Conda environment specification pinning GMT 6.0.0 with GDAL, GEOS, Ghostscript and other native dependencies needed by the GMT scripts.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces the study of intermediate-depth seismicity beneath the Himalayas and explains that this repository holds Python and GMT scripts that reproduce the manuscript's figures. It also points to the QuakeML catalog on Zenodo and splits the instructions into a Python path and a GMT path, which structures the rest of this tour.

tour.title: Running the Python Scripts
tour.description: The Python README explains how to run the figure scripts, so it is the entry to the analysis half of the project. Reading it first tells you what environment and data the drivers expect before you open the code.

tour.title: Figures 5-9 Driver
tour.description: Figures_5-9.py is the main Python driver. It reads the Himalayan QuakeML catalog, defines study sub-regions, and calls into two plotting modules to produce the temporal and migration figures. It is the hub that the next steps fan out from.
tour.languageLesson: The driver imports helper modules and calls their functions in sequence, a simple script-as-orchestrator pattern common in scientific Python.

tour.title: Temporal and Migration Plots
tour.description: Building on the driver from Step 3, temporal_plots.py handles magnitude vs time, cumulative counts, inter-event times and frequency-magnitude analysis. migration_plots.py handles migration of seismicity along strike and dip cross-sections. Together they hold the analysis logic that Figures_5-9.py invokes.

tour.title: 3D Hypocenters: Figure 10
tour.description: Figure_10.py is the second, independent Python driver. It renders 3D plots of earthquake hypocenters and stations using ObsPy, complementing the 2D and temporal views from the previous step.

tour.title: Supporting Analysis
tour.description: These auxiliary scripts plot the 1D velocity models used for earthquake location and summarize catalog details such as depth histograms. They provide the context for judging how reliable the catalog behind the main figures is.

tour.title: GMT Environment and Setup
tour.description: The second half of the project builds map-based figures with GMT. The GMT README gives short setup and run instructions, and gmt5.yml pins the conda environment (GMT 6.0.0 with GDAL, GEOS and Ghostscript) so the shell scripts behave reproducibly.
tour.languageLesson: A conda environment YAML pins package versions so that others can recreate the same toolchain.

tour.title: Study-Area Maps
tour.description: Figure_1.sh draws the overview map of the Himalayan region with topography, and Figure_2.sh maps the deep earthquake events. These scripts show the basic GMT pattern of building a map from layered data, which the cross-section scripts then reuse.
tour.languageLesson: GMT scripts are shell scripts that chain gmt commands such as basemap, grdimage and plot, each adding a layer to one PostScript figure.

tour.title: Depth Cross-Sections
tour.description: Figure_3AB.sh and Figure_3CD.sh project NLL and HypoDD hypocenter locations onto depth cross-sections. Comparing the two location methods shows how relocation sharpens the picture of intermediate-depth seismicity.

tour.title: Station Lists
tour.description: The GMT scripts plot seismic stations read from text files. all_stations.txt combines all networks, and the per-network files (for example HiCLIMB, HIMNT, NAMASTE and HiKNet) record the deployments used in the study.

tour.title: Earthquake and Focal Catalogs
tour.description: Complementary catalogs give the maps context. These include relocated events from the Gansser network, HIMNT events, the ISC catalogue, and a listing of focal mechanism catalogs.

tour.title: Faults and Color Palette
tour.description: Himalayan fault traces from HimaTibetMap come as GMT multisegment files for thrust, normal, dextral and sinistral faults, documented by their README. The him.cpt palette maps elevation to topographic colors for the maps.
tour.languageLesson: GMT multisegment files separate line segments with '>' header lines, and a CPT file maps data values to colors.
